- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.5) mid-period, model often overshoots downward; adjust forecast upward to avoid premature correction.
- After a recent spike (e.g., >75.0), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions to 5–10% of spike magnitude.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model exhibits mean-reversion bias; smooth transitions toward historical mean rather than extreme forecasts.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 1–2% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 2–3% for 3–5 days ahead.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment is clearly trending; if sentiment is flat, assume mild mean reversion, not abrupt direction change.
